title: Chapter 15: Landlord
html:
Chen Ge’s first impression of Wang Qi was simple: exhausted, sluggish, and weak. As they passed each other, Chen Ge returned the notice he had picked up. Wang Qi thanked him in a wavering voice—the first time Chen Ge had heard him speak. His voice was rough and gravelly, making the words slightly difficult to understand.

“You’re welcome.” Chen Ge smiled, then followed the limping man upstairs.

The second floor was even more dilapidated than the first. It was dark and damp, cobwebs filled the corners, and deep gouges scarred the walls. The limping man led Chen Ge to the far end of the corridor, unlocked the final door, and returned with a long ring of keys. “One night is fifty yuan. Pick any room you like on this floor.”

“Fifty yuan? That’s too expensive!”

“My apartments are the only place to stay for several kilometers. You should be grateful I’m charging only fifty.” As he spoke, the landlord kept glancing over his shoulder, as though checking for something behind him.

“Fine, but why do I have to stay on the second floor? Are the rooms on the first and third floors unavailable?”

“Why do you have so many damn questions? They’re off-limits, that’s why!” The limping man snatched the fifty yuan from Chen Ge and shoved a random key into his hand. “The room number is on the key. Find it yourself.”

Then he hurried back into his room. The moment the door began to close, Chen Ge heard a muffled, raspy sound from an old man inside. Frowning, he put a hand against the door. “Wait a second.”

“What now?!” the limping man asked with annoyance.

Chen Ge glanced through the narrow opening. The room looked small. Besides the limping landlord standing at the door, an elderly man sat in a wheelchair with his back to the corridor. He was probably the source of the sound Chen Ge had heard.

“I’m pretty thirsty. Do you have a vending machine or anything like that?”

“No!”

“Man, is this how you treat a customer…”

The door slammed in his face, leaving Chen Ge alone in the corridor with his suspicions deepening.

In a normal apartment building, reception would be near the entrance. Here, it was not only on the second floor but all the way at the far end of the corridor.Looking at the key in his hand, Chen Ge found himself with even more questions. Why are the first and third floors off-limits? And who is the old man staying with the landlord?

The key was marked 208. Coincidentally, the room was directly beside the landlord’s.

Whatever. I should put my things down first.After two hours on the road, Chen Ge was more than a little tired. The moment he opened the door, a heavy smell of mildew hit him. The room had clearly been vacant for a long time: dust coated almost every surface, and strange patches of fungus had spread across the bed.

Is this bed even usable?Before Chen Ge could even set down his backpack, a loud crash came from next door, like a plate shattering. He closed his door and pressed an ear to the wall. Soon he heard the landlord cursing angrily. His accent suggested he was not originally from the area.

The old man answered in a weak murmur. The landlord continued scolding him for several minutes before falling silent. Then, to Chen Ge’s confusion, the television volume suddenly rose.

What’s going on? What is he doing? Why did he turn the television up?Chen Ge listened for more clues, but the television drowned out everything else. Eventually, he gave up. Forget it. I should worry about myself. I doubt I’ll get much sleep tonight.

Chen Ge checked the supplies in his backpack and kept his phone close at hand. The online complaint mentioned suspicious stains beneath the paint and a terrible smell at night. But I searched everything I could find about Ping An Apartments, and there was no record of any murders here.

Still, Ping An Apartments had to contain some secret if the black phone had chosen it as a mission location. Chen Ge carefully inspected every corner of his room but found nothing unusual. It was an ordinary guest room in terrible condition, nothing more.

Since the landlord only rents rooms on the second floor, those rooms are probably the safest. Otherwise, he wouldn’t let guests stay here. If I want to find out what’s really happening, I need to look at the first or third floor.The Trial Mission would not officially begin until 11:00 p.m., leaving him another three hours. Not wanting to waste them, Chen Ge put his things away and quietly moved toward the door.

He wrapped his hand around the doorknob and began to open it, then froze halfway. His palm turned clammy, and a chill ran down his spine.

The limping landlord was standing directly outside. How long he had been there, Chen Ge had no idea.

The landlord clearly had not expected Chen Ge to open the door either. For a moment, the two men simply stared at each other in surprise.

“Landlord, why are you standing outside my room?” Chen Ge narrowed his eyes. The longer he stayed here, the more uneasy the man made him.

“Didn’t you say you were thirsty? I brought you this.” The landlord set a thermos of warm water beside Chen Ge’s door, his expression painfully unnatural.

“Thank you.” Chen Ge pretended not to notice the odd behavior and pulled the thermos inside. “Anything else?”

“No. Get some rest.” The landlord glanced into the room before adding, almost to himself, “There are no lights in the corridors, so it gets very dark after sunset. You’d better stay in your room at night.”

He turned away. Chen Ge did not relax until he heard the neighboring door close.

The landlord is quick-tempered and awkward, but I shouldn’t mistake his limp for weakness. He knocked Wang Qi off balance easily enough earlier.

Chen Ge was no detective. All he could do was compare what he had seen at the apartments with the countless mystery stories and crime dramas he had encountered before. He’s secretive, easily angered, and he was just standing outside my door. That makes him suspicious—but I might be jumping to conclusions.

Chen Ge put the thermos aside, and a troubling question occurred to him. If the landlord really is the murderer, does that mean I have to spend the entire night in the room next to his?

The thought made Chen Ge’s skin crawl. For all he knew, the man could spend the night lurking outside his door, waiting for an opportunity to make a move. Worse, as the landlord, he presumably had spare keys and could enter any room in the building.
